Chairman, Power Development Board, Dhaka and others
Vs.
Md. Fazlul Haque
full_judgment:
Mohammad Fazlul Karim, J: This appeal arose out of leave to appeal granted by this Court to consider the submission of the learned advocate of the appellant that there being no requirement in sub-rule (2) of rule 143 of the Bangladesh Power Development Board (Employees) Service Rules, 1982 to submit reply to the authority, High Court Division acted illegally in holding that respondent was seriously prejudiced in defending himself in the proceeding as he was directed to submit his reply to the enquiry officer, Tapan Kumar Das, appointed under sub-rule (3) of rule 143 in violation of sub-rule (2) of the said rule 143. 

 4. Mr. Md. Amir Hossain, the learned Advocate-on-Record appearing for the appellant, submits that the High Court Division acted illegally in holding that the direction to the delinquent to file the written statement to one Tapan Kumar Das, the enquiry officer, was contrary to the provision of sub-rule (2) of rule 143 as the same was to be submitted to the authority and as such the authority neither called for any written defence nor considered the same, rather directed the respondent to submit his reply to the enquiry officer, which has seriously prejudiced in defending himself in the proceeding and in gross violation of rule 143 of the Bangladesh Power Development Board (Employees) Service Rules, 1982. 

 5. Sub-Rule 1, 2 and 3 of Rule 143 of Power Development Board (Employees) Service Rules, 1982 runs as follows:- 

 "143. (1) When an employee is to be proceeded against under Clause (a) or (b) or (c) or (d) of Rule 138, he shall be called upon to submit explanation in writing to the authority within seven days as to why disciplinary action should not be taken against him for the alleged offence. 

 6. On perusal of the aforesaid sub-rule (1) of rule 143 it appears that an employee shall be called upon to submit explanation in writing to the authority within seven days as to why disciplinary action should not be taken against him for the alleged offence. But when the explanation of the employee is not found satisfactory than the sub-rule (2) intervenes whereupon the authority shall frame a charge and call upon him to submit a written defence within such period as may be specified in this behalf being not less than seven days and more than fourteen days, stating whether he desires to be heard in person. Sub-rule (1) specifically provides that the explanation is to be submitted to the authority in writing within 7 days, but sub-rule (2) provides that the authority shall frame a charge and call upon him to submit a written defence, but no authority or anybody has been mentioned therein to whom the written defence has to be submitted. On perusal d sub-rule (2), the logical conclusion that could be drawn is that the written defence has to be submitted to the enquiry officer stating whether he deserves to be beard in person. Sub-role (2) provides that the enquiry officer appointed by the competent authority shall conduct an enquiry into the charges giving the employee a personal hearing, if desired by him. 

 7. In view of the above, the High Court Division erred in law in holding that the respondent is entitled to get another show cause notice by the authority to submit written defence to them as per sub-rule (2) of rule 143 and that not having been given there was gross violation of the said rule. 

 Thus the finding of the High Court Division that the respondent is entitled to get another show cause notice by the authority to submit written defence as per sub-rule (2) of rule 143 of the Service Rules is set aside as not being the contemplation of the provision.
